7_harness_drive_mode.design_point: LLM-coordinated file-based handoff -- drive CLI yields at every Phase A halt to let researcher/planner/feature-author (Claude Code itself) author brief.md, plan.md, and goals[].feature_ids
7_harness_drive_mode.phase_a_notes: Three sequential halts. Each unblocked by Claude writing the artifact (researcher -> brief.md, planner -> plan.md, feature-author -> spec.yaml.goals[].feature_ids).
7_harness_drive_mode.phase_b_halt_detail: gate_0 on F-008 produced 'skipped' 2 times in a row with no detectable progress -- yielding
7_harness_drive_mode.phase_b_gate_results: skipped (no test command detected -- no package.json/pyproject/Makefile in cell)
7_harness_drive_mode.note: harness drive's Phase A is the dominant cost in this XL cell -- 3 halts * Claude authoring time = ~110 s wall clock. Phase B halted at the first feature because no toolchain was detected (cladding cell also skips gates, but its loop treats skip as non-fail). Different design choice, not a failure mode: harness drive favors progress detection over throughput. The richer signal lands once the target project has a real test runner.
